title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, and point auditors to archived artifact paths and SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent→configuration translators in NetOps workflows. Incorrect or out-of-order configuration commands can cause outages or policy violations; therefore, production designs frequently interpose deterministic validators and repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite broad architectural adoption, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted model, limited automated repairs) is rare. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types remain after automated repairs? Our contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces, complete provider-call accounting, and publicized cryptographic digests to enable forensic recomputation of contingency tables and per-episode traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators (e.g., header-space analysis, VeriFlow) provide canonical safety checks for configuration pipelines. Recent LLM→NetOps studies (NetConfEval and surveys of LLM-enabled configuration generators) typically report model accuracies or task-level leaderboards but often lack preregistration, paired designs, or archived validator traces. Our study differs in four ways: (1) a paired within-task comparison that holds the LLM initial candidate constant (shared_initial generation), (2) use of a deterministic validator that produces canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks recorded per episode, (3) a bounded adapter contract that permits at most one automatic repair call per task, and (4) full cryptographic hashing of principal artifacts (model calls, validator traces, task manifests, and analysis outputs) so auditors can reconstruct all reported counts deterministically. Representative prior artifacts: header-space analysis overview, VeriFlow, and recent NetConfEval-style NetOps evaluations provide the technical lineage supporting our validator and scoring choices.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design (N=200 intent→configuration tasks) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable error). The preregistered statistical test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI was specified (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistration contains sampling stratification plans (preregistered strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67), adapter contract, retry/missingness rules, and a multiplicity plan (one primary confirmatory hypothesis). The preregistration SHA-256 is 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract and model configuration. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so each task supplied a single initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded scoring. The adapter allowed at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, which matches model_calls_used = 201 in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02).

Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. We used a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor intent bank produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), allowed_touched_fields, and a required_sequence. The validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor-syntax constraints and intent-constraint checks, applies dependency/workflow policies, and executes deterministic simulator-backed semantic checks. The validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score ∈ {0,1} under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are the authoritative records; representative scoring examples and hashes are archived in the evidence bundle.

Execution, retry, and missingness procedures. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two automatic retries for provider-call failures; unresolved provider-call failures would be excluded from the primary paired analysis per the missingness plan. No provider-call failures occurred in this run. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200 (execution manifest SHA-256 referenced above; missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c).

Scoring, contingency accounting, and analysis executor. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced (a) the contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), (b) exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and (c) paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). The archived contingency CSV ordering is header 'guarded,baseline,count' (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0); we define n_11 as guarded=1 & baseline=1, n_10 as guarded=1 & baseline=0 (guarded-only improvements), n_01 as guarded=0 & baseline=1 (baseline-only improvements), and n_00 as both invalid.
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All counts, CI, and p-values are archived and hashed.

Interpreting the preregistered hypothesis algebra. The preregistered hypothesis was stated in relative terms (H1: ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate). Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction on that baseline corresponds to an absolute reduction of 0.0025 (i.e., from 0.005 to 0.0025). Our primary_estimand is the absolute paired difference in success rates (guarded_success − baseline_success) which equals +0.005 here because success increased from 0.995 → 1.000. Mapping between actionable-error reduction and success-rate difference is straightforward but sensitive to baseline prevalence: actionable_error_guarded = 1 − guarded_success, so relative reductions in error map to tiny absolute success-rate changes when errors are rare. The preregistered power was sized for large absolute effects (MDE ≈ 0.15), hence the observed rare-failure regime (baseline error = 0.005) renders the preregistered confirmatory threshold underpowered. We therefore conclude that the preregistered H1 (as sized) is not supported despite an observed guarded improvement; this is a power/estimand alignment issue rather than a computation error.

Representative discordant pair accounting. The run produced a single discordant pair in the direction of improvement (n_10 = 1) — i.e., an episode where the initial shared LLM candidate was scored invalid by the deterministic validator but the guarded pipeline returned a valid final configuration. The existence and per-episode validator traces for this discordant improvement are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json under execution/scoring/; auditors can deterministically recover the exact episode identifier and full validation trace using the archived files (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02 and execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a). Because the explicit episode id string is not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text, we provide these authoritative artifact pointers and hashes rather than inventing the id inline. The single discordant-improvement record is archived in the provider-call accounting and per-episode scoring JSONs.

Secondary and exploratory outcomes. The preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 (residual error-type distribution among guarded failures) could not be evaluated as a confirmatory test because guarded residual failures = 0. Exploratory diagnostics applied clustering of validator failure messages across the archive; contamination scans (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222) show no systematic contamination clusters. Missingness/exclusions: none (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c).
sections.discussion:
Operational implications. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and single automated repair), the guarded pipeline delivered a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In operational terms, the absolute benefit of inserting a deterministic validator is governed primarily by baseline LLM error prevalence, the validator's semantic coverage, repair budget (number of automated attempts), and the relative cost of residual failures. Where baseline errors are rare, large investments in validator-and-repair machinery yield small absolute reductions in misconfigurations; conversely, in higher-error regimes or in high-impact tasks, deterministic validation can materially reduce operational risk.

Design, estimand, and power lessons. Our preregistered power calculation targeted a large absolute effect (detect absolute reduction ≈0.15) and hence assumed substantially larger baseline error mass than observed. The observed baseline actionable-error rate (0.005) implies that detecting a 50% relative reduction would require substantially larger N or oversampling of high-difficulty tasks. Practical follow-ups: (1) increase N; (2) enrich the sample with higher-difficulty tasks where baseline errors occur more often; or (3) adopt alternative estimands (e.g., expected cost-weighted failures or rare-event risk metrics) better aligned to operational risk.

Reproducibility and forensic traceability. We archived cryptographic hashes for all principal artifacts so auditors can reproduce every reported number deterministically. Key authoritative digests (preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4; model configuration SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a). Auditors can recompute per-vendor observed stratified counts and retrieve the explicit discordant episode id by accessing execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 digests above) together with the per-episode scoring JSONs in execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json).

Reviewer-requested per-vendor numbers and discordant episode id. Reviewers requested (i) verbatim per-vendor stratified observed counts and (ii) the explicit discordant episode identifier. These values are deterministically recoverable from the archived execution files (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a plus execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02 and execution/scoring/*.json), but the explicit observed per-vendor numbers and the episode id string do not appear verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text. To preserve forensic traceability we therefore provide authoritative artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests rather than invent inline numeric assertions or identifiers that are not present verbatim in the archived text. Auditors wishing these verbatim values can deterministically extract them from the archived files using the provided digests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (sized for absolute effects ≈0.15) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed. All primary artifacts, per-episode validator traces, and analysis outputs are archived with cryptographic hashes to permit forensic recomputation. Future work should broaden model families, diversify validators, increase repair budgets, and target higher-difficulty or production-realistic task distributions to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair yields large absolute operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.
